title: Runtime suture: resolve session heap desynchronization causing cross-environment GPU OOMs and cache corruption
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments reported recurring GPU OOM waves followed by silent inference errors and, in some cases, corrupt model key-index lookups. Investigation shows a session heap desynchronization between the allocator's slab bookkeeping and the session-level key-index snapshot. The mismatch leads to dangling KV pointers and sporadic double-free/ghost page conditions that manifest as fragmentation and sudden per-node OOMs under long-lived streaming workloads. This ticket tracks the diagnosis, targeted runtime patch ("suture"), test plan, and canary/rollout schedule.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a long-running hosted session with streaming output (variable sequence lengths, many prefixes).
2) Stress with mixed small/big batches and intermittent model variants to exercise allocation paths.
3) Simulate session handoff (move session between worker processes) and force compact/evict cycles.
4) Observe allocator slab index deltas diverging between session metadata and global slab map (use /metrics/heap-snap).
5) Trigger until a GPU OOM or silent inference error occurs (typically after 10-100k tokens under heavy churn).
mitigation_and_workaround: Short-term: 1) Apply per-node eviction throttle and aggressive session reclamation (config flag runtime.eviction_force_reclaim=true) to avoid slab drift. 2) For Dedicated/Private customers hit hard, schedule rolling worker restarts during low-traffic windows to clear allocator state. 3) Temporarily disable session handoff optimizations (runtime.session_handoff=false) for affected clusters. These reduce incident frequency but do not address pointer desync permanently.
root_cause_summary: Root cause is an allocator epoch mismatch: the session-level KV index snapshot used during live inference was not stamped with the same allocation epoch as the underlying slab allocator when handoffs/compactions occurred. When a background compaction reclaimed a slab that a session still referenced (because its snapshot lacked the new epoch), subsequent allocations re-used freed memory in ways that produced silent corruption or immediate OOMs. Race windows are small but amplified by variable-length streams and cross-worker handoff.
proposed_fix_summary: Implement an 'allocation epoch stamp' and a lightweight session reclamation fence: 1) Stamp session snapshots with allocator epoch and verify on every handoff/restore; 2) Make compactor operations honor in-use epoch ranges (avoid reclaiming slabs until all epochs referencing them are advanced); 3) Add a defensive pointer-check and metrics emission when a session restores against a mismatched epoch. The change is localized to the runtime allocator and session restore path and includes a safe fallback to force a session rehydrate (drop KV snapshot) instead of resuming when mismatch is detected.
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy runtime-2.3.0-canary to 1% of hosted traffic and a single Dedicated pool (low-traffic) for 48 hours.
Ramp: if no regressions, ramp canary to 25% (hosted) and two Dedicated pools, monitor for 72 hours.
Full: full rollout to hosted and Dedicated pools with a scheduled weekend for Private customer coordination; provide a pre-rollout opt-in patch for Private/on-prem installations.
Rollback: runtime provides a fast-fallback path that forces session snapshot rehydrate; rollback target is previous runtime-2.2.x.
Migration: instrument migration tool to add epoch stamping to existing persisted snapshots where feasible; otherwise mark snapshots as needing rehydrate on next restore.
testing_plan: Unit: allocator epoch stamping unit tests and pointer-sanity asserts under randomized free/alloc workloads.
Integration: session handoff harness reproducing cross-worker restore while compaction runs concurrently.
Stress: multi-hour stress job in staging with mixed sequence lengths and bursty traffic to validate no OOM regression.
Customer QA: private customer test fixture (air-gapped) to validate patch prior to on-prem rollout.
